svg.aria-label: What to say when someone discloses violence, and what not to do. Five things to say, in order: I believe you. This is not your fault. Are you safe right now? Here is who I would have to tell. What would you like to happen next? Then seven things not to do: do not publish her story, do not confront the person responsible, do not push reconciliation, do not demand proof, do not comment on her clothing or behaviour, do not promise secrecy you cannot keep, and do not take over. The five sentences take about two minutes, require no training, and are most of the job.
svg.text: Five sentences. About two minutes. No training required.
SAY THESE, IN ROUGHLY THIS ORDER
Out loud, in those words, early. You are not a court.
She has already been told otherwise. Contradict it plainly.
The only urgent question. Tonight, that house, the children.
“Here is who I would have to tell.”
Before she tells you more. A disclosure she was tricked into is not consent.
“What would you like to happen next?”
Then start from her answer, not your plan. “Nothing yet” is a valid answer.
Publish her story · confront the person responsible · push reconciliation · demand proof
Comment on her clothing, movements or marriage · promise secrecy you cannot keep
Take over. The one thing she has been deprived of is control over what happens to her.
